fields.study_design: documentary descriptive analysis of regulator and sector statistics (self-described basic, quantitative, non-experimental, descriptive); no sampling or data-collection procedure beyond document review
fields.population: urban water and sewerage service users served by the 50 municipal EPS and SEDAPAL in Peru; documents: regulatory framework (tariff and service-quality regulations), SUNASS benchmarking, press and legal sources
fields.sample_size: 51 urban sanitation companies (50 municipal EPS plus SEDAPAL) in the SUNASS benchmarking; no household or complaint-level sample
fields.effect_measure: descriptive indicators from regulator benchmarking (coverage, continuity, pressure, water losses, metering, average tariff, pipe breaks, complaints); no inferential statistics
fields.effect_estimate: SUNASS reports 3.3 million Peruvians without a public water network and 6.4 million without sewerage connections (about 10% and 23% of the population). Urban coverage peaked at 92.5% for water and 85.9% for sewerage in 2017; average water losses are 37% (31.4% at SEDAPAL, about 42% at the other 49 EPS); micrometering reaches 75% of users on average (60% excluding SEDAPAL, with some EPS below 50%); the weighted average water tariff is S/ 2.941 per m3; pipe breaks fell from 22,101 in 2017 to 17,524 in 2022; 443,673 complaints were registered in 2022 and about 10% of users complain at least once a year despite a tedious procedure; continuity examples: 6 hours a day at EPS SEDAJULIACA and 3.7 hours at EMAPAVIGS. The author interprets the complaint volume as a sign of weak management and calls for investment (19.5 billion soles for water and 15 billion for sewerage over 30 years) and public-private partnerships.
fields.section: Full text (Spanish, 15 pages): Introduction; Materials and methods; Results (Tables 1-2, Figures 1-8); Discussion; Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Results text on Figures 1-8 (coverage, losses, metering, tariff, pipe breaks, complaints); Conclusions; Revista Dilemas Contemporaneos 12(1) art. 60

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a documentary descriptive analysis of national sanitation-sector indicators and the regulated complaints process in Peru; read in full text 2026-10-04. Descriptive statistics only; no empirical design for the complaints process itself.
